primary.$description:
The base neutral surface. Varies by theme and, in dark, by brand. The default page background, and the fill of anything that sits on top of the page.

Used in:
Page background, cards, dropdown, menu, popover, tooltip, toast, the content area of a modal, drawer or bottom sheet, and the rest fill of a floating secondary button of any sentiment, under that sentiment's weak hover on pointer-over — a secondary button that does not float has no fill. On top of the page, a card or menu is separated by its elevation.* shadow and color-border.static.secondary, not by its fill.

Do not:
Do not use it to set a region apart on the same plane — that is color-surface.static.secondary.

secondary.$description:
A neutral background one step below primary. It sets a region apart without lifting it, and can serve as the page when the screen needs a grey ground.

Used in:
A grey page background, a filter bar, a grouped block inside a card, a read-only field. On a secondary page, cards and panels take primary.

Do not:
Do not use it to lift an element off the page: it is darker than primary in both themes — that is color-surface.static.primary with elevation.raised or elevation.floating. Do not use it for a sentiment — that is color-surface.static.<sentiment>.weak or .strong.

tertiary.$description:
The most recessed neutral background, two steps below primary. It can also serve as the page when the screen needs a deeper grey ground; which grey the page takes is the designer's choice.

Used in:
A grey page background, wells, the track behind a progress bar or slider, an inset region inside a secondary area. On a tertiary page, cards and panels take primary.

Do not:
Do not use it to lift an element off the page: it is darker than primary and secondary in both themes — that is color-surface.static.primary with elevation.raised or elevation.floating. Do not use it for a sentiment — that is color-surface.static.<sentiment>.weak or .strong.

inverse.$description:
Background that contrasts against the rest of the UI.

Used in:
Tooltip body, neutral toast, high-contrast tag. Pair with color-content.static.on-inverse and color-border.static.on-inverse.

Do not:
Do not use it on large areas — this is a spot treatment. And do not put color-content.static.primary on top of it: inverse surfaces take on-inverse.

weak.$description:
Tinted brand fill for a surface that does not respond to the pointer.

Used in:
A brand alert banner, a weak brand tag, a list row carrying brand meaning. Pair with color-content.static.brand when the surface IS the message, or color-content.static.primary when it merely carries a sentiment. color-content.static.primary, color-content.static.secondary and the content of its own sentiment pass contrast here; color-content.static.tertiary does not.

Do not:
Do not use it on interactive elements. Hover and selected belong to color-surface.interactive.brand.weak.*.

strong.$description:
Solid brand fill for a surface that does not respond to the pointer. Identical in light and dark — it must stay dark enough to carry white content.

Used in:
A filled brand badge or tag. Small elements only. Pair with color-content.static.fixed-white, always, in every sentiment and theme.

Do not:
Do not use it on cards, panels, or any surface taller than ~48px — see brand-mass. And do not pair it with any content token other than color-content.static.fixed-white.

weak.$description:
Tinted accent fill for a surface that does not respond to the pointer.

Used in:
An accent alert banner, a weak accent tag, a list row carrying accent meaning. Pair with color-content.static.accent when the surface IS the message, or color-content.static.primary when it merely carries a sentiment. color-content.static.primary, color-content.static.secondary and the content of its own sentiment pass contrast here; color-content.static.tertiary does not.

Do not:
Do not use it on an element that responds to the pointer. That is color-surface.interactive.accent.weak.default, which resolves to this same tint and has hover, selected and selected-hover siblings this token has not.

Do not:
Do not use it on interactive elements. There is no color-surface.interactive.info family, so a hover or selected state cannot be built from this token.

highlight.$description:
Tinted fill marking a fragment of content rather than a component.

Used in:
Search-result matches, user text selection. Any color-content.static.* is guaranteed to pass contrast on it.

Do not:
Do not use it on component backgrounds. This is an inline text treatment.

overlay.$description:
Semi-transparent scrim behind a modal surface: color.neutral.900 at opacity.overlay, so it carries the brand's neutral tint. It separates the active surface from the content underneath and blocks interaction with it.

Used in:
The layer behind dialogs, modals, drawers and bottom sheets. The container it holds uses color-surface.static.primary.

Do not:
Do not use it on decorative overlays, image scrims, or any layer that does not signal a modal state.

default.$description:
Rest state of a subtle neutral interactive surface. Optional: bind it when the component has hover or selected states, so a state change is a single variable swap, or skip it to let the parent surface show through. It is translucent — a tint of the neutral ramp at opacity.default, a step off whatever sits behind it — so binding it is not a no-op. Varies by theme: the step and the amount change.

Used in:
List row, dropdown item, tab, chip, pill, table row. Pair with the hover, selected and selected-hover siblings of this same ramp.

Do not:
Do not use it as the rest fill of a floating secondary button — that is color-surface.static.primary. Do not bind it over color-surface.static.tertiary: in light it resolves to that same colour there and the state disappears. Interactive neutral rows sit on color-surface.static.primary or .secondary. Do not stand it in for background/transparent from another library. That one really is transparent and will not follow the theme.

hover.$description:
Hover on a subtle neutral interactive surface: a light step of the brand's neutral ramp at opacity.hover. Translucent, so it composites over whatever sits behind it — the page, an alert, a card. Varies by theme: the step flips with the ramp and the amount, opacity.hover, is lower in light.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of list row, dropdown item, tab, chip, pill, table row, neutral secondary or tertiary button. Pair with weak/default at rest, or with color-surface.static.primary on a floating secondary button — or with nothing at rest, letting the parent surface show through — and weak/selected when the choice persists.

Do not:
Do not bind it over color-surface.static.tertiary: in light it resolves to that same colour there and the state disappears. Interactive neutral rows sit on color-surface.static.primary or .secondary. Do not express selection with it. Hover is transient and selected is persistent — that is weak/selected.

selected.$description:
Persistently selected subtle neutral surface: a brand tint at opacity.selected, translucent so it composites over whatever sits behind it. Varies by theme. Selected exists only on weak — on a strong fill the fill itself already is the selection.

Used in:
Selected pill, selected list row, checked dropdown item. Small surfaces only. Pair with weak/selected-hover on pointer over, and with color-border.interactive.neutral.selected.

Do not:
Do not use it on cards, tiles or panels. A large selected surface keeps color-surface.static.primary and carries the state on its border plus a small brand indicator — see brand-mass.

selected-hover.$description:
Hover over an already selected subtle neutral surface: the same brand tint at opacity.selected-hover, more opaque than weak/selected, so it darkens in light and lightens in dark.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to weak/selected. Pair with weak/selected at rest.

default.$description:
Solid neutral interactive fill at rest, the neutral primary button. Varies by theme: it flips with the page — dark in light mode, light in dark — the way color-surface.static.inverse does, which is why its ink is color-content.static.on-inverse and not color-content.static.fixed-white.

Used in:
Neutral primary button, bold neutral control. Small elements only. Pair with color-content.static.on-inverse.

Do not:
Do not use it on cards, panels, or any surface taller than ~48px — see brand-mass.

hover.$description:
Hover on a solid neutral interactive fill. Varies by theme: it steps one further away from the page in each, so color-content.static.on-inverse keeps its contrast.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to strong/default. Pair with color-content.static.on-inverse.

selected.$description:
Solid neutral fill in its selected state. Visually identical to strong/default on purpose: on a strong surface the fill itself already is the selection. It exists so a bound token never has to be swapped when the component becomes selected.

Used in:
A selected bold neutral control. Pair with color-content.static.on-inverse.

Do not:
Do not read it as a hover token. Hover is strong/hover.

default.$description:
Rest state of a subtle brand interactive surface. Optional: bind it when the component has hover or selected states, so a state change is a single variable swap, or skip it to let the parent surface show through. It is opaque and already tinted at rest, so binding it is not a no-op — it resolves to the same tint as color-surface.static.brand.weak.

Used in:
Checked checkbox or radio, an item selected with brand emphasis. Pair with the hover, selected and selected-hover siblings of this same ramp.

Do not:
Do not stand it in for background/transparent from another library. That one really is transparent and will not follow the theme. Do not use it as the rest fill of a brand secondary button — a secondary button has no rest fill, and a floating one takes color-surface.static.primary; only its hover is on this ramp.

hover.$description:
Hover on a subtle brand interactive surface: a tint of its ramp at opacity.hover — built from the ramp step of color-surface.interactive.brand.weak.selected in light and of color-surface.interactive.brand.weak.selected-hover in dark — so pointer-over darkens in light and lightens in dark, over its own rest tint or over color-surface.static.primary. Translucent, so it composites over whatever sits behind it. Varies by theme: the step and the amount change, and the amount, opacity.hover, is lower in light.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of brand secondary or tertiary button, checkbox or radio, an item hovered with brand emphasis. Pair with weak/default at rest — or with nothing at rest, letting the parent surface show through, or with color-surface.static.primary on a floating secondary button — and weak/selected when the choice persists.

Do not:
Do not express selection with it. Hover is transient and selected is persistent — that is weak/selected. Do not put color-content.static.brand on it over the tinted weak/default in light: it is about 4.3:1 there, so that label takes color-content.static.primary.

selected.$description:
Persistently selected subtle brand surface. Selected exists only on weak — on a strong fill the fill itself already is the selection.

Used in:
Selected pill, selected list row, checked dropdown item. Small surfaces only. Pair with weak/selected-hover on pointer over, and with color-border.interactive.brand.selected.

Do not:
Do not use it on cards, tiles or panels. A large selected surface keeps color-surface.static.primary and carries the state on its border plus a small brand indicator — see brand-mass.

selected-hover.$description:
Hover over an already selected subtle brand surface.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to weak/selected. Pair with weak/selected at rest.

default.$description:
Solid brand interactive fill at rest. Varies by theme: one step deeper in dark than in light, so its hover can lighten there while color-content.static.fixed-white, always white, keeps AA. The sentiment's own colour is the fill, so white content on it clears AA.

Used in:
Checked checkbox or radio, the small brand indicator on a selected card or tile. Small elements only. Pair with color-content.static.fixed-white. A checkbox, radio or indicator sitting straight on the page also takes color-border.interactive.brand.selected: in dark the fill alone does not clear 3:1 against the page.

Do not:
Do not bind it on the brand primary button — that takes button.color-surface.primary.default, which a brand can override. Do not use it on cards, panels, or any surface taller than ~48px — see brand-mass.

hover.$description:
Hover on a solid brand interactive fill. Varies by theme: darker than rest in light, lighter than rest in dark, where the rest sits a step deeper; white content keeps 4.5:1 in both.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to strong/default. Pair with color-content.static.fixed-white.

Do not:
Do not bind it on the brand primary button — that takes button.color-surface.primary.hover.

selected.$description:
Solid brand fill in its selected state. Visually identical to strong/default on purpose: on a strong surface the fill itself already is the selection. It exists so a bound token never has to be swapped when the component becomes selected.

Used in:
Checked checkbox, active radio, the small brand indicator on a selected card or tile. Pair with color-content.static.fixed-white, and with color-border.interactive.brand.selected when it sits straight on the page: in dark the fill alone does not clear 3:1 against the page.

selected-hover.$description:
Hover over an already selected solid brand surface. Same step as strong/hover, so interactive feedback stays consistent.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to brand/strong/selected. Pair with color-content.static.fixed-white.

default.$description:
Rest state of a subtle accent interactive surface. Opaque and already tinted at rest, so it resolves to the same colour as color-surface.static.accent.weak. Varies by theme: the step flips so the tint stays the quiet end of the accent ramp in both.

Used in:
An accent-toned pill or list row. Optional — bind it when the component has hover or selected states, so a state change is a single variable swap, or skip it to let the parent surface show through. Pair with the hover, selected and selected-hover siblings of this same ramp.

Do not:
Do not reach for it for the main call to action — that is color-surface.interactive.brand.strong.default. Accent is the brand's second colour, not its primary one. Do not use it as the rest fill of an accent secondary button — a secondary button has no rest fill, and a floating one takes color-surface.static.primary; only its hover is on this ramp.

hover.$description:

Used in:
The pointer-over state of an accent secondary or tertiary button, an accent pill or row. Pair with weak/default at rest — or with nothing at rest, letting the parent surface show through, or with color-surface.static.primary on a floating secondary button — and weak/selected when the choice persists.

Do not:

selected.$description:
Persistently selected subtle accent surface. Selected exists only on weak — accent has no strong interactive ramp, so a selected accent element is always this one. Varies by theme: the step flips with the ramp.

Used in:
Selected pill, selected list row, checked dropdown item carrying accent meaning. Small surfaces only. Pair with weak/selected-hover on pointer over, and with color-border.interactive.accent.selected.

Do not:
Do not use it on cards, tiles or panels. A large selected surface keeps color-surface.static.primary and carries the state on its border plus a small indicator — see brand-mass.

selected-hover.$description:
Hover over an already selected subtle accent surface. Varies by theme: the step flips with the ramp.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to weak/selected. Pair with weak/selected at rest.

Do not:
Do not use it as the resting selected colour — that is color-surface.interactive.accent.weak.selected. This step only shows while the pointer is over an element that is already selected.

primary.$description:
Primary body text and icons.

Used in:
The default for any label, value or icon on a neutral surface, and the label of a neutral secondary or tertiary button. Pair with color-surface.static.primary, secondary or tertiary.

Do not use it on a strong fill, which takes color-content.static.fixed-white, or the inverse surface, which takes color-content.static.on-inverse.

secondary.$description:
Supporting text and icons. Varies by theme: a mid-grey ink in light, a light one in dark. It is below AA by design on tinted fills. In light: between 3.1:1 and 4.4:1 on color-surface.static.highlight and on the color-surface.interactive.*.weak selected and selected-hover fills, short of the 4.5:1 of SC 1.4.3. The low end is the selected-hover fill of brand, accent, positive, warning and danger. In dark it is about 4.1:1 on color-surface.static.highlight and on the color-surface.interactive.*.weak selected-hover fill of brand, accent, positive, warning and danger. It meets AA everywhere else.

Used in:
Descriptions, helper text, metadata, and neutral chrome inside a coloured component — the close icon of a sentiment alert stays secondary. On the tinted fills above it is accepted for supporting text only. Pair with color-content.static.primary as its sibling.

Do not:
Do not use it for information the user needs to read first — that is color-content.static.primary, which meets AA on every fill above.

tertiary.$description:
Faintest neutral text and icons, below AA by design on part of the scale: 3.5:1 on color-surface.static.primary and 4.2:1 on .secondary, short of the 4.5:1 of SC 1.4.3; about 5:1 on .tertiary. Varies by theme: a light-grey ink in light, a mid-grey one in dark.

Used in:
Only where the text is not what the user needs to read: the placeholder of an input whose label stays visible, and the text of a disabled control that is repainted rather than faded with opacity.disabled. Neutral surfaces only — color-surface.static.primary, .secondary and .tertiary. Pair with color-border.static.tertiary.

Do not:
Do not use it for anything the user has to read — metadata, helper text, captions, icons that carry meaning — that is color-content.static.secondary. Do not use it as the only label of an input. Do not use it on a tinted or inverse surface: those take color-content.static.primary and color-content.static.on-inverse.

rating.$description:
Fill of a rating star, filled and empty alike. Below AA by design in light: 1.8:1 on color-surface.static.primary, 1.6:1 on .secondary and 1.5:1 on .tertiary, short of the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11; above 7:1 on every neutral surface in dark. Decorative — it conveys nothing on its own, so the rating must also be written out as a number beside the stars. Identical in light and dark, and fixed across brand and viewport: a rating star is the same gold everywhere, and nothing about it changes with the surface behind it.

Used in:
The stars of a star rating, and nothing else: filled and empty stars both take it, and the icon style tells them apart. The numeric value beside them carries the rating and is color-content.static.secondary, which holds AA.

Do not:
Do not use it for anything that carries meaning — a warning, a favourite that toggles state, a highlighted row. A sentiment is color-content.static.warning; a chart series is color-data.yellow.strong. And never on a star row with no number next to it: the stars would then be the information, and at this contrast they cannot carry it — write the rating out in color-content.static.secondary.

brand.$description:
Brand text or icon that does not change with state. Sentiments carry no weak/strong on content — a low-contrast variant would be an accessibility bug, not a design option.

Used in:
The icon and text of a brand alert, a brand helper message, a brand outline tag, and the label and icon of a brand secondary or tertiary button, whose state lives on its surface. Pair with color-surface.static.brand.weak, color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.default, or with no fill at all.

Do not:
Do not use it on content sitting on top of a strong fill — that is always color-content.static.fixed-white. Reach for color-content.interactive.brand.* only when the text itself changes with state — a link, an active tab, a selected item. Do not put it on color-surface.interactive.brand.weak.selected-hover, or on weak.selected in light: it falls below 4.5:1 there, so text on those fills takes color-content.static.primary.

accent.$description:
Non-interactive accent text or icon. Sentiments carry no weak/strong on content — a low-contrast variant would be an accessibility bug, not a design option.

Used in:
The icon and text of an accent alert, an accent outline tag. Pair with color-surface.static.accent.weak, or with no fill at all.

Do not:
Do not look for an interactive twin: there is no color-content.interactive.accent, which is reserved for link-like content in brand and danger only. If the element is hoverable, carry the state on color-surface.interactive.accent.weak.* or color-border.interactive.accent.* instead. Do not put it on color-surface.interactive.accent.weak.selected-hover, or on weak.selected in light: it falls below 4.5:1 there, so text on those fills takes color-content.static.primary.

info.$description:
Non-interactive info text or icon. Sentiments carry no weak/strong on content — a low-contrast variant would be an accessibility bug, not a design option.

Used in:
The icon and text of an informational alert, an info outline tag. Pair with color-surface.static.info.weak, or with no fill at all.

Do not:
Do not look for an interactive twin: there is no color-content.interactive.info. If the element is hoverable, carry the state on its border or surface instead.

positive.$description:
Positive text or icon that does not change with state. Sentiments carry no weak/strong on content — a low-contrast variant would be an accessibility bug, not a design option.

Used in:
The icon and text of a success alert, a success helper message, a positive outline tag, and the label and icon of a positive secondary or tertiary button, whose state lives on its surface. Pair with color-surface.static.positive.weak, color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.default, or with no fill at all.

Do not:
Do not look for an interactive twin: there is no color-content.interactive.positive. If the element is hoverable, carry the state on its border or surface instead. Do not put it on color-surface.interactive.positive.weak.selected-hover, or on weak.selected in light: it falls below 4.5:1 there, so text on those fills takes color-content.static.primary.

warning.$description:
Non-interactive warning text or icon. Below AA by design in light: 3.7:1 on color-surface.static.warning.weak and on color-surface.static.tertiary, 4.1:1 on color-surface.static.secondary, short of the 4.5:1 of SC 1.4.3; 4.6:1 on color-surface.static.primary. It meets AA in dark. Sentiments carry no weak/strong on content.

Used in:
The icon and text of a warning alert, a warning helper message, a warning outline tag. Pair with color-surface.static.warning.weak, or with no fill at all. In light its text is limited to short text beside the warning icon — an alert title or a helper message — so the icon also carries the warning; longer or icon-less text takes color-content.static.primary.

Do not:
Do not look for an interactive twin: there is no color-content.interactive.warning. If the element is hoverable, carry the state on its border or surface instead. Do not put it on color-surface.interactive.warning.weak.selected-hover, or on weak.selected in light: it falls below 4.5:1 there, so text on those fills takes color-content.static.primary. Do not use it in light for text the user must read first on color-surface.static.warning.weak — that is color-content.static.primary.

danger.$description:
Danger text or icon that does not change with state. Sentiments carry no weak/strong on content — a low-contrast variant would be an accessibility bug, not a design option.

Used in:
The icon and text of an error alert, a field error message, a danger outline tag, and the label and icon of a danger secondary or tertiary button, whose state lives on its surface. Pair with color-surface.static.danger.weak, color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.default, or with no fill at all.

Do not:
Do not use it on content sitting on top of a strong fill — that is always color-content.static.fixed-white. Reach for color-content.interactive.danger.* only when the text itself changes with state — a destructive standalone link. Do not put it on color-surface.interactive.danger.weak.selected-hover, or on weak.selected in light: it falls below 4.5:1 there, so text on those fills takes color-content.static.primary.

on-inverse.$description:
Content sitting on an inverse surface — color-surface.static.inverse and the neutral primary button's color-surface.interactive.neutral.strong.*. Flips between themes because those surfaces flip.

Used in:
Tooltip label, neutral toast text and icons, high-contrast tag label, the label of a neutral primary button. Pair with color-surface.static.inverse, color-surface.interactive.neutral.strong.* and color-border.static.on-inverse.

Do not:
Do not use it on any other surface.

fixed-white.$description:
Ink for a fill that stays dark in both themes. White always — identical in light, dark and every brand: the fill under it does not move with the theme, so its ink must not either. The ink a light fill takes is color-content.static.fixed-black.

Used in:
The label and icons of any sentiment strong fill — color-surface.static.brand.strong and color-surface.interactive.brand.strong.default among them — and of a brand primary button through button.color-content.primary, and the label of a solid tag on color-data.*.strong, the same ink in both themes: 4.6:1 in light and 3.7:1 in dark, below AA by documented exception. It is the constraint that forces every sentiment strong fill to stay dark.

Do not:
Do not use it on a fill lighter than ramp step 500 — that is color-content.static.fixed-black, with one documented exception, color-data.*.strong, which stays at 3.7:1 in dark (orange 3.7:1 in light and 3.1:1 in dark), below SC 1.4.3 — or on a weak fill or a plain neutral surface, which take color-content.static.primary. And not on the inverse surface or on color-surface.interactive.neutral.strong.default, which both take color-content.static.on-inverse.

fixed-black.$description:
Ink for a fill that stays light in both themes. Black always — identical in light, dark and every brand: the fill under it does not move with the theme, so its ink must not either. The ink a dark fill takes is color-content.static.fixed-white. It holds AA on ramp steps 450 and lighter — a fill at step 500 or darker takes color-content.static.fixed-white instead.

Used in:
The label and icons of a brand primary button whose brand pinned the fill to a light ramp step, through button.color-content.primary, and of any component-tier fill pinned the same way.

Do not:
Do not use it on a sentiment strong fill — those stay dark and take color-content.static.fixed-white — or on a weak surface, whose ink is color-content.static.primary or the sentiment's own. Do not reach for it to darken content on a neutral surface either — that is color-content.static.primary.

default.$description:
Interactive content that represents the brand colour, for text or an icon that itself changes with state.

Used in:
Brand link, active tab label. Pair with color-content.interactive.brand.hover and /selected.

Do not:
Do not use it on content sitting on top of a brand fill — that is color-content.static.fixed-white. Do not put it on color-surface.interactive.brand.weak.selected-hover, or on weak.selected in light: it falls below 4.5:1 there, and a selected label is color-content.interactive.brand.selected. Do not use it on the label of a secondary or tertiary button, whose state lives on its surface — that is color-content.static.brand, as is any other brand text that does not change with state.

hover.$description:
Hover state of interactive brand content.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to color-content.interactive.brand.default.

selected.$description:
Persistently selected interactive brand content. There is no selected-hover on content — text colour does not change when hovering something already selected.

Used in:
Active tab label, the label and icon of a selected card or tile, selected nav item. Pair with color-border.interactive.brand.selected on a tab or nav item, and with color-border.interactive.neutral.selected on a selected card or tile.

Do not:
Do not use it on the label of a selected pill, which stays neutral — that is color-content.static.primary.

default.$description:
Interactive content that represents a destructive action, for text that itself changes with state.

Used in:
Destructive standalone link. Pair with color-content.interactive.danger.hover and /selected.

Do not:
Do not use it on the label or icon of a destructive secondary or tertiary button — that is color-content.static.danger; a destructive primary button takes color-content.static.fixed-white. And do not use it for content on top of a danger fill, which is color-content.static.fixed-white. Do not put it on color-surface.interactive.danger.weak.selected-hover, or on weak.selected in light: it falls below 4.5:1 there, and a selected label is color-content.interactive.danger.selected.

hover.$description:
Hover state of interactive danger content.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of a destructive standalone link.

selected.$description:
Persistently selected interactive danger content. There is no selected-hover on content — text colour does not change when hovering something already selected.

Used in:
A destructive item that stays chosen, such as a selected destructive row or menu entry. Pair with color-border.interactive.danger.selected.

primary.$description:
Strongest neutral border that does not change with state. Below the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11 by decision — about 1.8:1 in light and 2.8:1 in dark against color-surface.static.primary: it is decorative, so wherever it outlines something another cue identifies or separates it too — a change of surface, an elevation shadow, spacing, or a visible text label.

Used in:
A hard outline that is not a control, the progress track of a neutral toast, and the outline of a secondary button, which keeps the same border in every state and sentiment and is identified by its label. Pair with color-surface.static.primary or secondary — the first is also the fill of a floating secondary button.

Do not:
Do not use it where the border is what identifies the control or changes with its state — an input, a selectable container, a control with no visible text. That is color-border.interactive.neutral.*, which meets 3:1.

secondary.$description:
Supporting border and dividers. Decorative: it is never the boundary of anything on its own, so whatever separates the two regions has to come from somewhere else too — a change of surface, an elevation shadow, spacing.

Used in:
Dividers between list rows, section separators, the underline of an inactive tab. Pair with color-content.static.secondary.

Do not:
Do not use it on the divider of a hovered or selected row. Hover steps down to color-border.static.tertiary, selected steps to color-border.interactive.brand.selected on an active row. And do not use it for the boundary of a control, which is color-border.interactive.neutral.*.

tertiary.$description:
Faintest border. Decorative: it is never the boundary of anything on its own, so whatever separates the two regions has to come from somewhere else too — a change of surface, an elevation shadow, spacing. In light it is the same colour as color-surface.static.tertiary, so there it adds nothing at all.

Used in:
The divider of a hovered row, the border of a disabled or read-only field. Pair with color-surface.static.primary or secondary. Text in a disabled field takes color-content.static.tertiary; the value of a read-only field stays readable, color-content.static.primary or secondary.

Do not:
Do not use it to outline a card or menu — that is color-border.static.secondary. Do not let it be the only edge of anything — no border in this family can be, so the division has to be carried by a surface or an elevation shadow as well. The boundary of a control is color-border.interactive.neutral.*.

brand.$description:
Non-interactive brand border. Below AA by design in light on the faintest fills: about 2.97:1 on color-surface.static.tertiary and on color-surface.static.brand.weak, just under the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11; 3.7:1 on .primary and 3.3:1 on .secondary. It meets 3:1 in dark. Flat like content — no weak/strong.

Used in:
A brand outline tag or badge, a brand decorative rule. Pair with color-content.static.brand.

Do not:
Do not use it on inputs or selectable containers — use color-border.interactive.brand.* there. On color-surface.static.tertiary or the brand weak fill in light, an edge that has to be found on its own takes color-border.interactive.brand.* where it exists, or moves to color-surface.static.primary.

accent.$description:
Non-interactive accent border. Below AA by design in light on the faintest fills: about 2.97:1 on color-surface.static.tertiary and on color-surface.static.accent.weak, just under the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11; 3.7:1 on .primary and 3.3:1 on .secondary. It meets 3:1 in dark. Flat like content — no weak/strong. As the progress bar of a toast it sits below 3:1 on color-surface.static.accent.strong in light by design (about 1.9:1); about 3.1:1 in dark.

Used in:
The progress bar of an accent toast — a decorative tint on color-surface.static.accent.strong, under 3:1 by design, since the toast's own text carries the message — and an accent outline tag or badge. Pair with color-content.static.accent.

Do not:
Do not use it on inputs or selectable containers. Those take color-border.interactive.accent.default, which has the hover and selected steps this token has not. Do not use it for a bar on a strong fill that has to be found on its own — that is color-border.static.on-strong. On color-surface.static.tertiary or the accent weak fill in light, an edge that has to be found on its own takes color-border.interactive.accent.* where it exists, or moves to color-surface.static.primary.

info.$description:
Non-interactive info border. Below AA by design in light on the faintest fills: about 2.97:1 on color-surface.static.tertiary and on color-surface.static.info.weak, just under the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11; 3.7:1 on .primary and 3.3:1 on .secondary. It meets 3:1 in dark. Flat like content — no weak/strong. As the progress bar of a toast it sits below 3:1 on color-surface.static.info.strong in light by design (about 1.9:1); about 3.1:1 in dark.

Used in:
The progress bar of an info toast — a decorative tint on color-surface.static.info.strong, under 3:1 by design, since the toast's own text carries the message — and an info outline tag. Pair with color-content.static.info.

Do not:
Do not use it on inputs or selectable containers. There is no color-border.interactive.info, so an element in this sentiment that needs states must carry them elsewhere. Do not use it for a bar on a strong fill that has to be found on its own — that is color-border.static.on-strong. On color-surface.static.tertiary or the info weak fill in light, an edge that has to be found on its own moves to color-surface.static.primary — info has no interactive border family.

positive.$description:
Non-interactive positive border. Below AA by design in light on the faintest fills: about 2.97:1 on color-surface.static.tertiary and on color-surface.static.positive.weak, just under the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11; 3.7:1 on .primary and 3.3:1 on .secondary. It meets 3:1 in dark. Flat like content — no weak/strong. As the progress bar of a toast it sits below 3:1 on color-surface.static.positive.strong in light by design (about 1.9:1); about 3.1:1 in dark.

Used in:
The progress bar of a positive toast — a decorative tint on color-surface.static.positive.strong, under 3:1 by design, since the toast's own text carries the message — and a positive outline tag. Pair with color-content.static.positive.

Do not:
Do not use it on inputs or selectable containers — use color-border.interactive.positive.* there. Do not use it for a bar on a strong fill that has to be found on its own — that is color-border.static.on-strong. On color-surface.static.tertiary or the positive weak fill in light, an edge that has to be found on its own takes color-border.interactive.positive.* where it exists, or moves to color-surface.static.primary.

warning.$description:
Non-interactive warning border. Below AA by design in light: 3.1:1 on color-surface.static.primary, 2.8:1 on .secondary and 2.5:1 on .tertiary and on color-surface.static.warning.weak, under the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11 on the last three. It meets 3:1 in dark. Flat like content — no weak/strong. As the progress bar of a toast it sits below 3:1 on color-surface.static.warning.strong by design: about 1.9:1 in light and 2.5:1 in dark.

Used in:
The progress bar of a warning toast — a decorative tint on color-surface.static.warning.strong, under 3:1 by design, since the toast's own text carries the message — and a warning outline tag. Pair with color-content.static.warning. Decorative there: the warning text or icon beside it carries the meaning, so the edge never has to be found on its own.

Do not:
Do not use it on inputs or selectable containers — use color-border.interactive.warning.* there. Do not use it for a bar on a strong fill that has to be found on its own — that is color-border.static.on-strong. On color-surface.static.tertiary or the warning weak fill in light, an edge that has to be found on its own takes color-border.interactive.warning.* where it exists, or moves to color-surface.static.primary.

danger.$description:
Non-interactive danger border. Below AA by design in light on the faintest fills: about 2.97:1 on color-surface.static.tertiary and on color-surface.static.danger.weak, just under the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11; 3.7:1 on .primary and 3.3:1 on .secondary. It meets 3:1 in dark. Flat like content — no weak/strong. As the progress bar of a toast it sits below 3:1 on color-surface.static.danger.strong in light by design (about 1.9:1); about 3.1:1 in dark.

Used in:
The progress bar of a danger toast — a decorative tint on color-surface.static.danger.strong, under 3:1 by design, since the toast's own text carries the message — and a danger outline tag. Pair with color-content.static.danger.

Do not:
Do not use it on inputs or selectable containers — use color-border.interactive.danger.* there. Do not use it for a bar on a strong fill that has to be found on its own — that is color-border.static.on-strong. On color-surface.static.tertiary or the danger weak fill in light, an edge that has to be found on its own takes color-border.interactive.danger.* where it exists, or moves to color-surface.static.primary.

on-inverse.$description:
Divider on color-surface.static.inverse, below AA by design: 1.9:1 against that surface, short of the 3:1 of SC 1.4.11. Decorative, like the other static borders — it is never the only thing separating two regions. Varies by theme.

Used in:
Separators inside a tooltip, a neutral toast, an inverse panel, where spacing or the content already separates the parts. Pair with color-surface.static.inverse and color-content.static.on-inverse.

Do not:
Do not use it as the only edge of something on an inverse surface — a boundary that must be seen there takes color-content.static.on-inverse as its stroke. Do not use it on color-surface.interactive.neutral.strong.*, which has no divider token yet.

on-strong.$description:
Divider on a sentiment strong fill.

Used in:
Separators inside a filled toast, badge or banner. Pair with a sentiment strong surface — color-surface.static.<sentiment>.strong or color-surface.interactive.<sentiment>.strong.<state> — and color-content.static.fixed-white.

Do not:
Do not use it on color-surface.interactive.neutral.strong.*, whose fill flips with the theme: this divider disappears into it in dark. That case has no divider token yet.

default.$description:
Rest border of a neutral interactive container, for a border that changes with state.

Used in:
Input, select, selectable card or tile, pill, chip. Pair with color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.default.

Do not:
Do not use it on static dividers or decorative rules — those use color-border.static.*. Do not use it on the outline of a secondary button: that border stays the same in every state, so it is color-border.static.primary.

hover.$description:
Hover border of a neutral interactive container.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of an input, a selectable card or tile. Pair with color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.hover.

selected.$description:
Selected border of a neutral interactive container, so the selection reads without the brand colour. Varies by theme. On a large surface this border is what carries the selection, so the surface itself can stay color-surface.static.primary — see brand-mass.

Used in:
Selected pill, selected card or tile, the border of a focused input or select. Pair with color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.selected on small surfaces, and with the focus.ring effect on a focused field.

Do not:
Do not use it for a selection that must carry the brand colour — that is color-border.interactive.brand.selected.

default.$description:
Rest border of a brand interactive container, for a border that changes with state.

Used in:
Checked checkbox or radio outline, an item selected with brand emphasis. Pair with color-surface.interactive.brand.weak.default.

Do not:
Do not use it on static dividers or decorative rules — those use color-border.static.*. Do not use it on the outline of a secondary button: that border stays the same in every state, so it is color-border.static.primary.

hover.$description:
Hover border of a brand interactive container.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of a brand-emphasis control. Pair with color-surface.interactive.brand.weak.hover.

selected.$description:
Selected border of a brand interactive container. On a large surface this border is what carries the selection, so the surface itself can stay color-surface.static.primary — see brand-mass.

Used in:
Active tab underline, the divider of an active row. Pair with color-surface.interactive.brand.weak.selected on small surfaces.

Do not:
Do not use it on a plain input, select, pill, card or tile — those take color-border.interactive.neutral.selected.

selected-hover.$description:
Hover over an already selected brand interactive container.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to color-border.interactive.brand.selected. Pair with color-surface.interactive.brand.weak.selected-hover on small surfaces.

Do not:
Do not use it on the pointer-over state of a container that is not selected — that is color-border.interactive.brand.hover.

default.$description:
Border of a control carrying accent meaning. Varies by theme: a lighter step in dark, where the same hue against a dark surface would sink into it.

Used in:
The outline of an accent-toned input, tag or selectable container. Pair with color-content.static.accent on the label, and with color-surface.interactive.accent.weak.default on the fill.

Do not:
Do not use it on an element that never responds to the pointer — that is color-border.static.accent.

hover.$description:
Hover border of a control carrying accent meaning. Varies by theme: it steps away from the surface in both, darker in light and lighter in dark.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to color-border.interactive.accent.default.

Do not:
Do not express a persistent choice with it — that is color-border.interactive.accent.selected.

selected.$description:
Focused or selected border of a control carrying accent meaning. Varies by theme: in light it takes the same step as hover, so the selection is carried by the fill and the focus ring; in dark it steps further from the surface.

Used in:
An accent field while focused, or a selected accent container. Pair with the color-focus.ring effect on the same node, and with color-surface.interactive.accent.weak.selected on the fill.

Do not:
Do not use it for a transient pointer-over — that is color-border.interactive.accent.hover.

selected-hover.$description:
Hover over an already selected accent border. Varies by theme: the furthest step from the surface in both.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of anything bound to color-border.interactive.accent.selected. Pair with color-surface.interactive.accent.weak.selected-hover on the fill.

Do not:
Do not use it as the resting selected colour — that is color-border.interactive.accent.selected.

default.$description:
Border of an input in a success state.

Used in:
The field outline when the field carries positive meaning. Pair with color-content.static.positive on the label and helper text; the fill stays color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.default.

Do not:
Do not tint the field surface to match. The sentiment lives on the border and the text.

hover.$description:
Hover border of an input in a success state.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of a positive field.

selected.$description:
Focused or selected border of an input in a success state.

Used in:
A positive field while focused. Pair with the color-focus.ring effect on the same node.

default.$description:
Border of an input in a warning state.

Used in:
The field outline when the field carries warning meaning. Pair with color-content.static.warning on the label and helper text; the fill stays color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.default.

Do not:
Do not tint the field surface to match. The sentiment lives on the border and the text.

hover.$description:
Hover border of an input in a warning state.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of a warning field.

selected.$description:
Focused or selected border of an input in a warning state.

Used in:
A warning field while focused. Pair with the color-focus.ring effect on the same node.

default.$description:
Border of an input in a error state.

Used in:
The field outline when the field carries danger meaning. Pair with color-content.static.danger on the label and helper text; the fill stays color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.default.

Do not:
Do not tint the field surface to match. The sentiment lives on the border and the text.

hover.$description:
Hover border of an input in a error state.

Used in:
The pointer-over state of a danger field.

selected.$description:
Focused or selected border of an input in a error state.

Used in:
A danger field while focused. Pair with the color-focus.ring effect on the same node.

ring.$description:
Outer band of the focus ring, the brand-coloured half of a two-colour indicator. Varies by brand through its primary ramp, and by theme: a light-mid step in light (primary.400), kept light on purpose because a darker step read as a heavy outline, and a lighter one in dark. In light it reaches about 3.1:1 (SC 1.4.11) against color-surface.static.primary and stays at about 2.8:1 against .secondary, below 3:1 by decision. In dark it reaches 3:1 against both.

Used in:
Only inside the focus.ring effect style, wrapped around color-focus.ring-inner. It is the band that carries the contrast against the page; the inner band keeps it apart from a strong fill of the same colour.

Do not:
Do not bind it alone as a stroke or a single shadow — apply focus.ring, which carries both bands. Do not vary it by sentiment. Do not rely on it alone on a surface other than color-surface.static.primary — on .secondary, .tertiary or a tinted fill check the ring against that surface, and do not darken the band to fix it there.

ring-inner.$description:
Inner band of the focus ring: the colour of color-surface.static.primary in each theme (the same value), so on that surface the gap between the element and color-focus.ring reads as background. Varies by theme.

Used in:
Only inside the focus.ring effect style, between the element's edge and color-focus.ring.

Do not:
Do not bind it on its own — apply focus.ring. Do not use it as a surface colour; a page surface is color-surface.static.primary.

halo.$description:
Wash layer of every elevation shadow — the wide, very faint halo that surrounds an element on all four sides and separates it from what is behind without drawing a line. Varies by theme: at a far higher alpha in dark, where a mid-neutral shadow on a dark surface would be invisible.

Used in:
The surrounding layer of elevation.raised and elevation.floating, on its own in the first and under color-shadow.ambient's drop in the second. Raise it to make the whole set more present, lower it to flatten it — without touching any geometry.

Do not:
Do not bind it to a layer. It is never used on its own: an element's shadow is an elevation.* effect style, and its fill is a color-surface.* token.

ambient.$description:
Falloff layer of every elevation shadow — the wider and fainter of its two drop layers, giving the element air under it. Varies by theme: darker and at a far higher alpha in dark, where a mid-neutral shadow on a dark surface would be invisible.

Used in:
The second layer of every elevation.* token, paired with color-shadow.halo in the first. Raise it to make the set airier, lower it to flatten it — without touching any geometry.

Do not:
Do not bind it to a layer. It is never used on its own: an element's shadow is an elevation.* effect style, and its fill is a color-surface.* token.

disabled.$description:
Layer opacity of a whole component in its disabled state — a percentage, which Figma's opacity variables read on their 0–100 scale. Fixed across brand and viewport; the same in light and dark.

Used in:
The root layer of any disabled control — buttons, inputs, list rows, chips — so text, icon and border fade together.

Do not:
Do not fade individual parts of a disabled control with their own opacity — apply this once on the root; content that only needs de-emphasis takes color-content.static.secondary instead.

overlay.$description:
Alpha of the modal scrim, as a percentage, like the rest of the opacity family. Not bindable and not published: it is the amount a colour token composites at, not a layer opacity a designer sets. Fixed across brand and viewport; varies by theme — higher in light, so the page behind recedes and the modal holds the focus, lower in dark, where the page is already dark and a heavier scrim would only turn it black.

Used in:
color-surface.static.overlay, as the alpha of its rgba(): in Figma the scrim is a composed colour variable that links this token, so editing it reaches the scrim.

Do not:
Do not set a layer's own opacity to it — a scrim is a colour, not a faded layer. Fading a whole component is opacity.disabled.

hover.$description:
Alpha of a hover state layer, as a percentage, like the rest of the opacity family. Not bindable and not published: it is the amount a colour token composites at, not a layer opacity a designer sets. Fixed across brand and viewport; varies by theme, lower in light than in dark. In light, sentiment and supporting text on a weak hover keep 4.5:1 over color-surface.static.primary and secondary.

Used in:
The alpha of every color-surface.interactive.*.weak.hover rgba(): in Figma each hover is a composed colour variable that links this token, so editing it reaches every hover.

Do not:
Do not set a layer's own opacity to it — a hover is a fill, not a faded layer. Fading a whole component is opacity.disabled.

default.$description:
Alpha of the rest state of a translucent interactive surface, as a percentage, like the rest of the opacity family. Not bindable and not published: it is the amount a colour token composites at, not a layer opacity a designer sets. Fixed across brand and viewport; varies by theme, and stays below opacity.hover in both.

Used in:
The alpha of color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.default.

Do not:
Do not set a layer's own opacity to it — a rest tint is a fill, not a faded layer. Fading a whole component is opacity.disabled.

selected.$description:
Alpha of the selected states of a translucent interactive surface, as a percentage, like the rest of the opacity family. Not bindable and not published: it is the amount a colour token composites at, not a layer opacity a designer sets. Fixed across brand and viewport; varies by theme, and stays below opacity.selected-hover in both.

Used in:
The alpha of color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.selected.

Do not:
Do not set a layer's own opacity to it — a selected tint is a fill, not a faded layer. Fading a whole component is opacity.disabled.

selected-hover.$description:
Alpha of the selected-hover state of a translucent interactive surface, as a percentage, like the rest of the opacity family. Not bindable and not published: it is the amount a colour token composites at, not a layer opacity a designer sets. Fixed across brand and viewport; varies by theme, and stays above opacity.selected in both.

Used in:
The alpha of color-surface.interactive.neutral.weak.selected-hover.

Do not:
Do not set a layer's own opacity to it — a selected tint is a fill, not a faded layer. Fading a whole component is opacity.disabled.
